scope: Telencephalic pathway proposals, checked 2026-10-04. Routes are teaching summaries, not measured streamlines; relay labels distinguish nerve/tract from synapse. Optional clinical features are not diagnostic rules.

sources.B-visual: Blumenfeld, Neuroanatomy through Clinical Cases, 2nd ed. (2010), pp. 463-476 (PDF pp. 489-502), Figures 11.6-11.8 and 11.15
sources.B-hippocampal: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 834-837 (PDF pp. 860-863), Figures 18.8, 18.11 and 18.13
sources.B-basal: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 748-752 (PDF pp. 774-778), Figures 16.5-16.8; textbook explicitly describes direct/indirect model as incomplete
sources.B-language: Blumenfeld, 2nd ed., pp. 885-887 and 894-897 (PDF pp. 911-913 and 920-923), Figure 19.2; language processing involves distributed reciprocal networks

pathways.name: Retina to visual cortex

steps.label: Retinal ganglion cells
steps.note: Axons carry retinal output; retinal surface is not separately modeled.

steps.label: Optic chiasm
steps.note: Nasal retinal fibres cross; temporal retinal fibres remain ipsilateral.

steps.label: Optic tract
steps.note: Each tract represents the contralateral visual hemifield from both eyes.

steps.label: Optic radiation
steps.note: Temporal Meyer's loop carries superior-field information; parietal route carries inferior-field information.

steps.label: Extrastriate processing
steps.note: V2 is one of several extrastriate areas; streams are interconnected rather than two isolated pipelines.

pathways.clinical: Unilateral postchiasmal injury may cause contralateral homonymous field loss; pattern depends on lesion extent. Macular sparing can occur in occipital infarction but is not obligatory.

pathways.name: Ascending auditory network

steps.label: Cochlear nuclei
steps.note: Dorsal cochlear nucleus also contributes; the diagram is a branched network, not one obligatory serial route.

steps.label: Superior olivary complex
steps.note: Receives bilateral input via crossing and uncrossed projections; some cochlear projections bypass it.

steps.label: Lateral lemniscus
steps.note: Auditory information ascends bilaterally with contralateral predominance.

steps.label: Auditory radiation
steps.note: Separate tract mesh unavailable; passes through sublenticular internal capsule.

pathways.clinical: A unilateral lesion above the cochlear nuclei usually does not cause complete unilateral deafness. Bilateral central injury can impair hearing or auditory recognition.

pathways.name: Hippocampal intrinsic memory circuit

steps.label: Perforant pathway
steps.note: Layer II input to dentate/CA3; direct layer III input to CA1 forms a parallel route.

steps.label: Mossy fibres
steps.note: Axons of dentate granule cells.

steps.label: CA3
steps.note: Grouped CA2/CA3 atlas record is a display convenience; CA2 is not a compulsory relay of the trisynaptic route.

pathways.clinical: Medial temporal damage may impair formation of new declarative memories; outcome depends on bilateral extent and wider memory networks.

pathways.name: Papez memory circuit (simplified)

steps.label: Mammillothalamic tract
steps.note: Not separately modeled.

pathways.clinical: Fornical, mammillary or anterior thalamic injury can disrupt memory. This heuristic omits direct fornix-to-anterior-thalamus and many other reciprocal pathways; it is not an isolated emotion circuit.

pathways.name: Basal ganglia direct pathway (teaching model)

steps.label: Motor/premotor cortex
steps.note: Glutamatergic excitation of striatum.

steps.label: Striatal direct-pathway neurons
steps.note: GABAergic inhibition of GPi/SNr; dopamine generally facilitates D1-expressing neurons in this model.

steps.label: GPi/SNr output
steps.note: Reduced tonic inhibition can disinhibit motor thalamus; SNr is a parallel output nucleus.

pathways.clinical: The rate model helps explain movement selection but does not account for all firing patterns, tremor, dystonia or DBS effects.

pathways.name: Basal ganglia indirect pathway (teaching model)

steps.label: Motor/premotor cortex
steps.note: Excites striatal neurons.

steps.label: Striatal indirect-pathway neurons
steps.note: GABAergic inhibition of GPe; dopamine generally reduces D2-pathway activity in this model.

steps.label: GPe
steps.note: Reduced GPe inhibition disinhibits STN.

steps.label: STN
steps.note: Excites GPi/SNr. Verify root taxonomy ID before integration.

steps.label: GPi/SNr
steps.note: Inhibits motor thalamus.

pathways.clinical: Classical net effect suppresses competing actions; hyperdirect cortex-to-STN input and recurrent GPe-STN circuitry also contribute and are omitted here.

pathways.name: Dominant perisylvian language network

steps.label: Dorsal and ventral language connections
steps.note: Arcuate/SLF-related dorsal routes support auditory-motor integration and repetition; additional temporal-frontal routes support comprehension. Arcuate fasciculus is not identical to the entire SLF.

pathways.clinical: Left hemisphere is language dominant in most people, not all. Aphasia patterns depend on distributed cortical/subcortical damage, and the route is reciprocal rather than a single serial chain.
